newsitem.title: FINLAND: LITHUANIA-BBH, HANSA INVESTMENTS FORM FIRM WITH UTENOS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-BBH, HANSA INVESTMENTS FORM FIRM WITH UTENOS.

text.p: Hartwall on Monday confirmed that Baltic Beverage Holdings (BBH), owned with Norway's Orkla, was to form a company with Lithuanian brewer Utenos.
It also said that Estonian Hansa Investments would also have a stake in the new company.
Utenos earlier said its shareholders voted to form a joint company with BBH, rejecting a competing investment offer by Carlsberg .
The Lithuanians will hold 50 percent of the new company but Hartwall did not say how much of the remaining 50 percent would be owned by BBH and how much by Hansa Investments.
It said in a statement that BBH and Hansa would invest some $12.5 million in the Lithuanian firm.
"We have decided not to say (the exact stakes) at this stage," Hartwall's chief executive Jussi Lansio said by telephone.
"It is likely that our stake will rise in the future," he added.
Hartwall said Utena's capacity was some 70 million litres of beer and 20 million litres of soft drinks. It also had a malt house whose capacity was 12,000 tonnes a year.
The investment would upgrade its products and technology to international standards and boost Utena's brand names, Hartwall said in the statement.
The investment will be carried out over two years.
Hartwall said BBH's total sales would rise to 550 million litres in 1997.
